source_spans.quote: (a) Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator—

(1) No pilot may take off a U.S.-registered civil aircraft (except a free balloon that incorporates a basket or gondola, or an airship type certificated before November 2, 1987) unless the pilot in command of that aircraft ensures that each person on board is briefed on how to fasten and unfasten that person's safety belt and, if installed, shoulder harness.

claim_judgments.rationale: No supported contrast: the draft's stated applicability matches the source rule under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(1). The prohibition correctly binds the pilot from taking off without the required passenger briefing, preserving the exceptions for free balloons with baskets/gondolas and airships certificated prior to November 2, 1987, as well as the overarching Administrator authorization caveat.

source_spans.quote: (a) Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator—

(2) No pilot may cause to be moved on the surface, take off, or land a U.S.-registered civil aircraft (except a free balloon that incorporates a basket or gondola, or an airship type certificated before November 2, 1987) unless the pilot in command of that aircraft ensures that each person on board has been notified to fasten his or her safety belt and, if installed, his or her shoulder harness.

claim_judgments.rationale: No supported contrast: the draft's stated applicability matches the source rule under 14 CFR 91.107(a)(2). It accurately states that no pilot may cause a U.S.-registered civil aircraft to move on the surface, take off, or land without ensuring passengers are notified to fasten safety belts and shoulder harnesses if installed, subject to the standard balloon/airship exclusions and Administrator authorization.
